tasks.spec: You are THE pilot executor for jt-acculynx-mirror: you play staged writes from jt_mirror.pending_write into the live JobTread org 22PazeRM5FCH (Pro Exteriors) via the Pave API. This is the only task in this run and the only place JobTread mutations are allowed. BOUNDARY: mutations ONLY via the ops staged in pending_write rows (status='staged'); NEVER invent writes, NEVER create users/memberships/invites (hard seat rule), NEVER delete anything in JobTread, never write files except your deliverable /Users/chussey/Documents/a-roofers-open-brain/integrations/bridges/jobtread/mirror/b3-execute/execution-report.md, never log credential values. CREDS: set -a; source /Users/chussey/.config/cleverwork/master.env; set +a. REQUEST CONSTRUCTION: build EVERY request body with python3 (json.dumps on a dict) written to a temp file under /tmp — NEVER with jq or shell heredoc interpolation; a prior attempt corrupted a request via jq quoting and burned the canary. SCALE: this bulk round holds tens of thousands of staged rows. Write ONE resumable python driver script that processes every staged row in band order — resolving refs, calling Pave, updating pending_write/crosswalk/write_action_log after EACH write so an interruption resumes cleanly — and run it to completion; do NOT hand-process rows one LLM-turn at a time. Print progress to stdout every 200 writes. RESUME SEMANTICS: rows already status='executed' or 'skipped' are DONE — never re-execute them; process only status='staged' rows; the canary rule applies to the first staged customer_accounts row only if NO customer_accounts row is already executed — if one is, skip the canary step and proceed with ordered execution directly. Pave calls: POST https://api.jobtread.com/pave with JSON body {"query": {"$": {"grantKey": "<value of $JT_SUPABASE_MIRROR_GRANT_KEY>"}, "<op>": {"$": <input>, <response fields>}}} — always request the created entity's id back. Supabase SQL: curl -s -X POST https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/rnhmvcpsvtqjlffpsayu/database/query -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"<SQL>"}'. VERBATIM REQUEST TEMPLATES for the remaining domains (use EXACTLY these shapes; the response-selection key for create ops is 'created<Entity>', NEVER the bare entity name): createDocument: {"query": {"$": {"grantKey": K}, "createDocument": {"$": <the staged payload with refs resolved and __execution_order removed>, "createdDocument": {"id": {}}}}}. createDailyLog: {"query": {"$": {"grantKey": K}, "createDailyLog": {"$": <payload>, "createdDailyLog": {"id": {}}}}}. PER-JOB CLOSED-JOB BATCHING (documents and daily_logs): group all remaining staged rows by their target job. For each job: query its live closedOn via Pave ({"job": {"$": {"id": X}, "id": {}, "closedOn": {}}}); if closedOn is non-null, updateJob to closedOn null, then execute ALL of that job's staged documents and daily logs, then updateJob restoring the original closedOn; if closedOn is null, just execute the writes. This reopen dance already worked in the job_custom_values round — reuse it. If a write inside a reopened job still fails, record the row failed with the full error, RE-CLOSE the job anyway (never leave a job reopened), and continue. Pave input-shape reference: the scraped docs at '/Users/chussey/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox-AIA4/Cleverwork Main/GROK/Tools/catalog/jobtread/api/docs/' and README.md in that folder. UPDATE-OP SHAPE (canonical, proven): update ops take ALL inputs under "$" (id + fields), with response selection as a sibling key, e.g. updateJob: {"$": {"id": X, "customFieldValues": {fieldId: value}}, "job": {"$": {"id": X}, "id": {}}} — never put id at the selection level. CLOSED-JOB PROTOCOL: if updateJob returns a permission error ('You don't have permission to update this job') and that job's createJob payload carried closedOn (see the r3f fix-report Closed-Job Note), retry as a three-step sequence: (a) updateJob {"$": {"id": X, "closedOn": null}}, (b) the original customFieldValues update, (c) updateJob restoring the original closedOn value. If step (a) itself fails with a permission error, mark the row failed with error 'closed-job-locked (JT blocks API updates to closed jobs)' and CONTINUE with the remaining rows — this is a documented platform limitation, not a systemic halt condition. ALGORITHM: (1) Load staged rows ordered by (payload->>'__execution_order')::int, created_at. (2) CANARY FIRST: execute exactly ONE customer_accounts createAccount row, read it back by id from Pave, verify the name matches, record crosswalk + write_action_log. If the canary fails in ANY way: mark that row failed with the full error, execute NOTHING else, write your report, and exit nonzero — a failed canary must halt the pilot. (3) Execute ALL staged vendor_accounts rows (the bulk round un-deferred them; there is no cap). (4) For every other staged row in order: resolve every {"$ref": "<source_type>:<source_id>"} in the payload via jt_mirror.crosswalk (source_system+source_id -> jt_id); strip the __execution_order key; execute the op; on success set status='executed', jt_id=<returned id>, executed_at=now(), insert jt_mirror.crosswalk (source_system='acculynx' or as the ref type implies, source_id, source_table from source_ref, jt_type, jt_id, domain) and append jt_mirror.write_action_log (op, source_ref, jt_id, request summary WITHOUT grantKey, response status, created_at). On failure: status='failed', error=<response body excerpt>, continue — EXCEPT if the failure is an unresolvable $ref whose source band already ran, or 10 consecutive failures occur, in which case stop and report (systemic problem). (5) THROTTLE <=4 req/s (sleep 0.25s between Pave calls); on 429 back off with jitter and halve your rate for the next 100 calls. (6) Also mirror created entities into the jt_mirror read-back tables (accounts, locations, jobs, documents, cost_items, cost_codes, custom_fields) with id + name + raw response + synced_at where a matching table exists. (7) Final self-verification before writing your report: re-query Pave for 5 random created jobs by id and confirm echo-back; include the results. DELIVERABLE execution-report.md sections: ## Canary (op, id, read-back proof), ## Execution Summary (per-domain executed/failed/skipped counts from live SQL), ## Failures (every failed row: op, source_ref, error), ## Read-Back Sample, ## Verdict. HARD RULES: honest accounting — the report's numbers must come from live SQL, not memory; if the run is partial, say exactly where it stopped and why.
